paragraphs.text: Wellington IC R1465 of 22 Operational Training Unit, based at Wellesbourne Mountford, flew into the summit of Waun Rydd in the Brecon Beacons on 6 July 1942. It was on a training flight. The aircraft carried practice bombs and reconnaissance flares and flew into low cloud. The pilot is believed to have come down from the advised 10,000 ft to check his position. All five crew died.

The five were Canadians serving in the RCAF. They were Flight Sergeant John Beverley Kemp, the pilot, aged 21, from Oakville, Ontario; Ernest Edward Mittell, aged 22, of Clinton, Ontario; Kenneth Ferguson Yuill, aged 30, of Winnipeg; Harold Creighton Beatty, a wireless operator; and James Patrick Hayes, an air gunner, whose parents lived in Souris, Manitoba. All five are buried at Hereford Cemetery.
The wreckage was spread over a large area and has since been gathered into two piles. The site is a Controlled Site under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986.
A memorial cairn marks the site. The Coflein record says it was built by pupils and staff of Tredeger Comprehensive School. Walkers leave poppies, crosses and wreaths there.

notes: No IWM War Memorials Register entry found for this cairn (two web searches; results were unrelated). Crew role conflicts: Mittell is Observer (Coflein) vs Navigator (IBCC); Yuill is bomb aimer (Coflein) vs air observer (search excerpts of CVWM); rank for Kemp is Flight Sergeant (CWGC, ASN) vs Sergeant (Coflein). Coflein spells Mittell 'Mitell' and Yuill 'Yull'. TracesOfWar says six Canadians died; every other source says five. Several pages (CVWM, IBCC, ASN, canadianfallen) were read only as search-result excerpts because direct fetches returned 429/403/404 or failed DNS; re-check by hand. The older Ystradgynlais History page (http://www.ystradgynlais-history.co.uk/wellington-r1465.html) failed a TLS certificate check and was not read. IBCC Kemp page and CWGC pages for Mittell, Hayes and Beatty not located, so those links are omitted. 'Tredeger Comprehensive School' is Coflein's spelling; likely Tredegar, unconfirmed, and the school's role is single-source. Dedication date, inscription and current maintainer not found; the existing record's 'Brecon Royal British Legion' contact and 'Remembrance Weekend' event are unsupported by any source read. IWA and Wandering Welsh Girl share wording so are not independent. The IWA article says the official report is not given for R1465; an earlier search summary claiming 'crew error' relates to another crash.
